articleTitle: A Linear Simulation Technique for a Power Traveling-Wave Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This Paper discusses a simple linear simulation technique to optimize the design of a traveling-wave amplifier (TWA) for best power and efficiency while avoiding extensive non-linear simulations. This simple optimization is used in achieving an equal voltage swing across the drain of each FET cell of the non-uniform traveling wave amplifier, in addition each cell is matched to its optimum load impedance. This is demonstrated by designing a non-Uniform traveling wave power amplifier MMIC using this simple linear technique. This MMIC PA was fabricated using a $0.25\mu {\mathrm{m}}$ GaN/SiC process, it operates from DC to 10GHz and delivers 5W (37dBm) output power, 13dB small signal gain and a 25% PAE. Simulated results agree with measurements.

articleTitle: Harmonic-Injection Doherty Power Amplifier: Benefits and Limitations
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper presents an investigation into the effects of second harmonic ($2f_{0}$) power injection on the performance of a Doherty power amplifier (DPA). This investigation is conducted through the implementation of a single-stage 24 GHz harmonic-injection DPA (HI-DPA) manufactured on a 100 nm Gallium Nitride (GaN) technology. An on-chip injection power amplifier (IPA) operating at 48 GHz is used to generate the injected $2f_{0}$ power. On-wafer continuous wave measurements demonstrate that at 24 GHz, the HI-DPA achieves a power added efficiency (PAE) of 37% and 32.5% at a peak output power (POP) of 32.5dBm and 6 dB output power back-off (OPBO), respectively. When compared to a conventional DPA (CDPA) designed and manufactured under similar operating conditions, the HI-DPA exhibits an improved AM/PM characteristics with a 3.3% and 6% higher PAE at POP and OPBO at a cost of 1 dB small-signal gain penalty.

articleTitle: Robust Estimation for Digital Predistortion with Nonideal Equalization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper proposes a closed loop estimator that adapts a digital predistortion (DPD) module. DPD is used to compensate for nonlinearities in a RF power amplifier (PA). The standard method for a closed loop estimator is a least square approach. It can produce a biased estimate if the observation path is not equalized properly. A prior solution computes the error and basis signals within the estimator in the frequency domain and notches the linear bandwidth so that the coefficient estimate is based on the out-of-band signals, which are due exclusively to the nonlinearity. Unfortunately, this method cannot be used if the out-of-band signals are bandwidth limited within the observation path. The proposed approach also computes the estimator signals in the frequency domain. The linear frequency response from the input to the output of the observation path is estimated using a long-term average. It is used to remove the linear signal spectrum from the output leaving only the nonlinearity portion of the spectrum as an error signal. It is shown that improved DPD performance is achieved even when the frequency response of the observation path is nonideal.

articleTitle: A 2.6GHz broadband LDMOS Doherty Power Amplifier for Small-Cell Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper presents the design approach, realization, and measurement results of a 10W fully-integrated 2way Doherty Power Amplifier (DPA) for small-cell applications. The two stage PA MMIC was designed using LDMOS technology, fabricated with a size of $3 \times 3.3$ mm$^{2}$ and mounted in a $7 \times 7$ mm$^{2}$ LGA package. To meet our efficiency requirements, a 2-way asymmetrical DPA topology was selected. Using a pulsed continuous wave (CW) signal at 2.6GHz, the fabricated DPA achieves a 45-47% power-added efficiency (PAE) at 9dB output power back-off (OBO), a linear gain of 30dB and a peak power of 40dBm. In addition, thanks to the video bandwidth (VBW) optimization, the device shows strong linearity performances by achieving an adjacent channel leakage ratio (ACLR) after digital predistortion (DPD) better than -56dBc for 200MHz instantaneous bandwidth (IBW) and up to -49dBc for 400MHz IBW.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Coupling Between Passive Circuits and Non-Uniform Transistor Operation in High-Power Microwave Packaged Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper describes accurate modeling methodology for high-power microwave device with a saturated output power of 180 W, an operating frequency range of 3.4-3.8 GHz, and an internally pre-matched discrete device. First, an all-passive device is fabricated to verify simulation accuracy of passive circuits. Then, a packaged device with a GaN die was confirmed on accuracy of actual device. We have shown that the coupling between matching circuits inside the package has a large influence on the isolation characteristics, and that it is necessary to include all package circuit components in the simulation. Furthermore, we estimated accuracy degradation caused by non-uniform operation of unit FETs within a GaN die and provided a guideline for accurate modeling of high-power devices.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Output Power and Efficiency for a Set Noise-Power Ratio of a K-Band Power Amplifier By Means of Analog Pre-Distortion
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper investigates the output power and efficiency improvements in a K-band power amplifier (PA) that can be achieved using analog pre-distortion (APD). At first, the APD tuning voltage is optimized to maximize gain and phase flatness using Gaussian pulses. Next, the PA average output power is swept and the noise-power ratio (NPR) of a 750 MHz signal is measured with APD enabled and disabled. It is found that APD improves the PA average output power between 1 W and 1.6 W (or +2 dB) for NPRs between 16 and 29 dB. At the same time, APD improves PA efficiency by 1 to 7 percentage points (pp) for this 31 % peak-efficiency PA. These results suggest the use of APD for improving PA efficiency and output power.

articleTitle: Application of the Cardiff Model for Orthogonal LMBA Response Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper shows the ability of the Cardiff Behavioural Model to precisely reproduce the response of an advanced power amplifier architecture. The investigation involved varying the phase of the complex load on the isolated port of a 50 W orthogonal load-modulated balanced amplifier operating at 2.5GHz. Leveraging a limited set of data points, the Cardiff model effectively estimates the PA’s performance across a wide range, from approximately 10 dB output backoff to around 1-2 dB of gain compression, with a maximum normalised error of only −20 dB. This novel application of the Cardiff Model offers an efficient means of reducing measurement and simulation time for designing and optimizing this particular type of power amplifier.

articleTitle: Study of AM-PM Deviation on Power Amplifier Linearization Performances for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper presents an easy method to simulate the impact of a Doherty power amplifier (DPA) Amplitude to phase (AM-PM) deviation on its linearizability using digital predistortion (DPD) system. To simulate the DPD system, the DPA is replaced by its nonlinear impulse model extracted from continuous-wave (CW) simulation. The behavioral model identification data are modified in such a way to reduce or increase only the AM-PM dispersions. This technique and linearization performances are evaluated using a MMIC 75W 3-ways DPA at 3600MHz. The purpose of these simulations is to rapidly advise the designer of the maximum AM-PM deviation that a given DPD system can compensate for. The designer will then adjust the circuit accordingly to maximize the efficiency-linearity trade-off.

articleTitle: Broadband GaN Power Amplifier MMIC with a Nonuniform Transmission Line Output Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper presents the design and measured results of a GaN MMIC single-stage power amplifier (PA) with a broadband non-uniform microstrip line output matching network that results in 40% fractional bandwidth centered roughly at 20 GHz with a gain >8 dB. The synthesis of the non-uniform transmission line (NTL) and its integration with the PA bias line are discussed. A meandering technique is implemented to miniaturize the NTL footprint on the MMIC. Measurements agree well with simulations, showing >8 dB small-signal gain from 16 – 26 GHz for this single-ended single-stage PA.

articleTitle: Energy-efficient D-Band Power Amplifier Linearization Adopting Back-Gate Feedforward Technique in 22nm FD-SOI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This work presents a highly energy-efficient linearization technique for D-band power amplifiers (PA) in 22nm fully-depleted silicon-on-insulator (FD-SOI) technology. The nonlinear effects arising from the NMOS transistor transconductance are reduced by leveraging the back-gate terminal of the output stage devices, directly controlling the biasing point based on the input RF signal. A 2-stage PA has been designed to demonstrate the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed technique. The prototype 22nm FD-SOI CMOS PA delivers 10.2dB peak power gain, $\gt 11$ dBm saturated power (Psat) and a power-added-efficiency (PAE) of 6% at the 1dB output compression point (OP1dB) with an 0.8V supply centered at a carrier frequency of 150GHz. The adaptive back-gate feedforward loop improves the overall input 1dB compression point by 2.5dB while at the same time decreasing the third- and 5th-order intermodulation distortions across the entire bandwidth by 6dB and 10dB, respectively. Furthermore, the EVM is improved by 5.5 and 6.1 percentage points for a 10-MHz 5G NR 16-QAM and a 64-QAM signal, respectively.

articleTitle: Investigating Feeding Techniques for High-power and High-efficiency E-band Power Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: In this article, the feeding techniques for high-power and high-efficiency E-band (60–90GHz) power amplifiers (PAs) that employ high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) with a gate periphery of $8 \times 45 \mu \mathrm{m}$ are investigated. To enhance the performance of the HEMTs with extended periphery, a symmetrical gate feeder and a low-impedance drain feeder line are proposed for the input and output matching networks, respectively. A wideband three stage PA is demonstrated with an $8 \times 45 \mu \mathrm{m}$ HEMT at the final stage, utilizing IAF GaN 100nm technology. The measured PA delivers an output power of 28.7dBm associated with a power-added-efficiency (PAE) of 25.4% at 76GHz while maintaining a PAE above 20% from 70 to 80GHz. Moreover, the PA exhibits a small-signal gain of more than 19.5dB within the 49-79GHz range, featuring a 3-dB bandwidth of 30GHz. To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this is the first PA to demonstrate PAE exceeding 20% and covering the majority (70–80GHz) of the Satcom E-band.

articleTitle: High Accuracy DPD Approach for Hybrid Beamformer using Novel Training Symbol Mapping
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: Advantages of the higher frequencies used for mmWave 5G, make it suitable for providing high-speed connectivity in densely populated areas or supporting ultra-low latency applications. In this manuscript, a novel Scalable Training OFDM (ST-OFDM) signal is synthesized and used in conjunction with a digital pre-distortion routine to enhance the performance of a mmWave 5G hybrid beamforming array. The proposed method provides $\sim 4$ dBc of Adjacent Channel Power Ratio (ACPR) improvement compared to the popular average DPD technique.

articleTitle: An All-Analog Sampled-Line VSWR Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: A sampled-line reflectometer is presented that uses all-analog computation to produce a voltage proportional to the square of the load reflection coefficient, intended to be integrated into an RF front-end within an array. The novel approach for analog computation, and its dependence on sampler placement along the line is discussed. Experimental measurements of a varying load impedance are demonstrated using a microstrip line with diode samplers, operating at 3 GHz.

articleTitle: High-Efficiency GaN Doherty Power Amplifier based on Inverse Class-F Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper presents the design and characterization of a Doherty power amplifier based on high-efficiency continuous inverse class-F individual amplifiers. The prototype achieves a saturated output power in excess of 42.5dBm, with efficiency higher than 70% and 50%, at saturation and 6dB output back-off respectively, over the frequency band 1.45GHz–1.75GHz (18% fractional band). The good agreement between simulations and measurements and the comparison with the state of the art at similar frequencies demonstrate the potential of the application of harmonic tuning strategies to the Doherty architecture, despite the challenge of maintaining wideband operation.

articleTitle: Impact of Matching Networks on the Impedance Settling Time in High Frequency Power Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper presents a study on the settling time of the impedance loading the high frequency transistors in power amplifiers. Depending on the matching network type and complexity, the impedance can take significant time for settling. This will affect the ability of the power amplifier to respond to fast changing modulation signals or fast, short RF pulses, hence becoming a limiting factor for emerging wireless systems, alongside other effects such as bias networks and thermal response. The study is based on fitting the frequency domain response with a rational function, allowing the application of a sinewave stimulus starting at t =0 for evaluating the transient behavior. The results show that the settling time is not easily relatable to parameters usually considered such as the group delay, hence suggesting that full understanding of these effects will need deeper studies.

articleTitle: A Concurrent 2.45/5.8 GHz Power Amplifier with an Optimal Dual-band Matching Method
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This study presents the design and fabrication of a concurrent 2.45/5.8 GHz dual-band power amplifier (PA) with a dual-band matching method for optimized performance. The proposed matching method simultaneously utilizes series and parallel resonance to transform the frequency-dependent fundamental complex optimum load impedance to $50 \Omega$ at two arbitrary frequencies. Additionally, the selectable range of a low-frequency is analyzed when a high-frequency is selected. The dual-band PA was designed and fabricated on the Rogers 5880 substrate, utilizing the Wolfspeed GaN HEMT CGH40006s. Measurement results indicate that the implemented dual-band PA achieves a small signal gain of 13.9 dB at 2.45 GHz and 10.6 dB at 5.8 GHz. Furthermore, at the 3 dB compression point, the output power (OP$_{3dB})$ is measured at 38.4 dBm for 2.45 GHz and 38.6 dBm for 5.8 GHz, while the corresponding drain efficiency (DE$_{3dB})$ is 71 % at 2.45 GHz and 59.6 % at 5.8 GHz. OP$_{3dB}$ and DE$_{3dB}$frequency responses of the dual-band PA were above 38 dBm and 70 % between 2.4 GHz and 2.5 GHz, and over 38 dBm and 55 % from 5.7 GHz to 5.9 GHz, respectively.

articleTitle: A compact 27 dBm triple-stack power amplifier for 13 GHz operation in CMOS-SOI
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: Power amplifiers at 13 GHz are attracting attention for possible use in 6G wireless systems, and the comparison between different transistor technologies that could be applied is an emerging research focus. Relative to 5G mm-wave power amplifiers, higher output power (up to 30-35 dBm), high efficiency and high linearity are important requirements for 6G. This paper focuses on design considerations for high power CMOS-SOI technology at 13 GHz, including scaling issues relative to the well-studied 28GHz designs. A single-stage, single-ended pMOS amplifier is reported which achieves Psat=27 dBm and peak PAE=43%, in a small area (0.33 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> excluding pads). These are believed to be the highest reported results for CMOS, although this band has received relatively little attention to date.

articleTitle: A Compact 6–12 GHz MMIC Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This work presents the design and characterization of a MMIC power amplifier (PA) operating over 6–12 GHz. A three-stage low-pass input matching network and output matching network that incorporates the supply structure into the match enables a compact area of only 2 mm by 1.2 mm. The fabricated PA is measured in CW to have 35 dBm saturated output power with a PAE ranging from 35% to 45% over the octave band. CW measurements with varying supply voltage demonstrate efficiency enhancement at output power back-off. Modulated performance over the entire RF band is also reported.

articleTitle: Large-signal characterization and behavioral modeling of mm-wave GaN HEMT switches tailored for advanced power amplifier architectures
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper presents a characterization and modeling campaign on high-power microwave switches based on GaN High Electron Mobility Transistor (HEMT) structures. The large-signal characterization is performed at 30 GHz using load-pull, allowing for testing different terminations for the switch and hence emulating the different conditions in which it might be used. The experimental data obtained is used to extract a Cardiff behavioral model that automatically enables interpolation of the data where it is noisy, and its use in a CAD simulator. Having a model for the switch that captures the response in different conditions is particularly important to enable their use in designing advanced PA architectures that use tunable elements to achieve more flexible operation.

articleTitle: A Linearized Calibration Technique Using Modulated Signals for Wideband Dual-Input Doherty Characterization
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: A linearized calibration technique for wideband characterization of high-efficiency multiple-input transmitter architectures, such as Chireix, outphasing and dual-input Doherty power amplifiers is presented. The proposed three step calibration process, including digital predistortion, is demonstrated for a dual-input setup and 400MHz of signal bandwidth at 3.6 GHz. Simultaneous use of three receivers allows drifts of the measurement setup to be detected in-situ, increasing the reliability of results and protecting vulnerable devices under tests. Destructive interference of 20-MHz and 400-MHz modulated signals at the output of a quadrature hybrid is used to verify the calibrated measurement setup, achieving signal power levels of -37.6 and -23.1 dBc, respectively.

articleTitle: A Ku-band High Gain 40 W GaN HPA MMIC for Satellite Systems in a 0.25- μm GaN Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This study focuses on the design and validation of an internally matched high-power amplifier monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) for Ku-band solid-state power amplifier (SSPA) system integration. The designed MMIC exhibits sufficient power gain and output power characteristics, making it suitable for SSPA applications. The MMIC offers a compact and cost-effective SSPA configuration by reducing the number of components, such as gain blocks, isolators, and power combiners. The results show a performance of more than 40 W output power with a considerably high saturated power gain (greater than 22 dB) over the entire band (15.25–16.25 GHz).

articleTitle: Class S Power Amplifier System for Radio Applications in the HF Band
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This work presents the development and implementation of a class S power amplifier system for the use in radio applications in the HF band. The system consists of a bandpass $\Delta \Sigma$ modulator and a class D power amplifier system. Both parts are designed separately, so a flexible combination of the subsystems is possible, but the focus of this work are the mutual influencing factors of the two subsystems. The complete class S system shows a maximum drain efficiency of 13.3% at a SQNR of 37.9 dB. For better reconstruction of the input signal a simple filter and impedance matching circuit is added at the output. The measurement of the filtered signal yields a drain efficiency of 7.8% at a SQNR of 33.2 dB.

articleTitle: Ultra-Fast Operating Point Switching for Watt-Level 3.6 GHz Power Amplifiers
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: To enable micro sleeps of transmitters during network inactivity without forfeiting real-time capabilities, power amplifiers (PAs) with fast operating point switching (OPS) are required. In this paper, for the first time to the authors’ best knowledge, OPS is investigated for efficient watt-level power amplifiers and measured turn-on times are reported. Based on a compact bias switching network suitable for GaN amplifiers, two new PAs, one in class E and one in class AB, with saturated output power around 40 dBm and ultra-fast OPS capability are presented. Turn-on times below 37 ns are achieved and idle power less than 1 mW is measured, enabling even microsecond sleeps with minimal latency for significant energy savings.

articleTitle: Integrated GaN Power Detector for High Power Millimeter-Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper presents the design and measured performance of an integrated Gallium-Nitride-based power detector, which is tailored to monitor the output power of a state-of-the-art Gallium-Nitride high power amplifier in E-band (71-76GHz). To show the high power application, the temperature-compensated power detector is driven with a 1W millimeter-wave signal, which has not been shown before at frequencies in the range of 68-74GHz. The measured performance sets the state-of-the-art for integrated millimeter-wave power detection in terms of maximum detected power and shows the first on-chip integrated Gallium-Nitride millimeter-wave detector.

articleTitle: A 3.6GHz Highly Efficient Dual-Driver Doherty Power Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper presents an advanced Doherty-type power amplifier architecture, which uses two driver amplifiers embedded in the Main and Peaking paths of the Doherty stage. Due to the biasing configuration, the power consumption of the Driver stage is reduced in the back-off, enhancing the backoff efficiency, while improving the load modulation and the power utilization factor of the transistor devices of the power amplification stage. Some of the design trade-offs introduced by the Dual-Driver Doherty are discussed and investigated using a simplified transistor model. Finally, a demonstrator is designed using GaN-HEMT devices for all amplifiers and evaluated to investigate the performance of the line-up with modulated signals. The measured performance after digital pre-distortion using a 100MHz wideband signal centered at 3.6GHz, showed at an average output power of 40dBm a modulated line-up efficiency of 48% and an ACLR of -45dBc with average gain of 25.7dB.

articleTitle: A 22FDX® 2 Stack Power Amplifier for 5G Applications with 19dBm Psat and 49% Peak PAE
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: In this work, a 2 Stack cascode Power Amplifier (PA), for 5G applications at 28GHz has been designed and fabricated with 22nm FDX technology from GlobalFoundries. An enhanced device variant of Super Low Voltage Threshold (SLVT) called ENBFMOAT is used. The architecture of PA is based on pseudo differential 2 stack cascode with on chip input and output baluns. A new layout design style has been improved to mitigate the phase delays. Moreover, connecting the Nwell to front gate to strength the ground plane. A sandwiched output balun style is utilized to increase the coupling and reduce the loss. All these improvements provided us with 19dBm linear output power (P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf>) and peak Power Added efficiency (PAE) of 49%. The reliability for 10 years is also investigated and ensured the long life PA working time efficiently. To best authors knowledge, the presented PA introduced the highest PAE combined with P<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">sat</inf> in CMOS/SOI technology.

articleTitle: DPD Algorithm with Long-term Memory Effects Compensation for AlGaN/GaN HEMTs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE Topical Conference on RF/Microwave Power Amplifiers for Radio and Wireless Applications (PAWR)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for compensating long-term memory effects in AlGaN/GaN HEMTs power amplifiers using a two-dimensional local support interpolation technology with the Farrow structure. The proposed method is validated through linearization tests, and experimental results demonstrate an improvement of 7 dB in NMSE for E-TM3.1a TDD with long-term memory effects compensation. Additionally, the maximal EVM is reduced from 3.5% to 0.9% for E-TM2a FDD case and from 3.8% to 0.9% for E-TM2a FDD traffic variation case.
